# `silk/url/form`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read and write `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` text, the format of HTML form bodies and of
URL queries such as `a=1&b=two+words`.

## When to use
Use [`UrlForm.parse`](#UrlForm.impl.parse) to read the fields of a form body or a URL query, and
[`UrlForm.serialize`](#UrlForm.impl.serialize) to write them. The rules are those of the WHATWG URL Standard, which
JavaScript's `URLSearchParams` uses.

## Details
The text is split at `&`, and each part at its first `=`. Empty parts are skipped. In names and
values, `+` is a space and `%XX` escapes are decoded; invalid escapes stay as they are. The
decoded bytes are read as UTF-8, with U+FFFD for each invalid sequence.

## Examples
### Read and write a query
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.text.string { String }
import silk.url.form { UrlForm, UrlFormPair }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let pairs = run UrlForm.parse("q=silk+lang&page=2") |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if List<UrlFormPair>.length(&pairs) != 2 || String.view(&List<UrlFormPair>.asSlice(&pairs)[0].value) != "silk lang" {
    return 1
  }
  let text = run UrlForm.serialize(List<UrlFormPair>.asSlice(&pairs)) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if String.view(&text) != "q=silk+lang&page=2" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `UrlForm` with `import silk.url.form { UrlForm }`.

<a id="UrlForm.impl.serialize"></a>

### Associated function `serialize`

```silk
pub effect fn serialize(pairs: &[UrlFormPair]) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns `pairs` as form text: each name and value encoded, joined by `=`, and the pairs
joined by `&`.

#### Details
Space becomes `+`. Letters, digits, `*`, `-`, `.`, and `_` stay as they are, and every other
byte becomes `%XX`.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.
